newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Airlines profits up 10 percent.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Airlines profits up 10 percent.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp. said Thursday that it recorded a 10 percent rise in profits in the third quarter, despite the re-imposition of a federal ticket tax and a sharp rise in the cost of fuel.
The domestic and international air carrier said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 climbed to $253.9 million, or $3.15 a share, from $231.1 million, or $2.27 a share, a year ago.
Revenues for the quarter rose 7 percent to $2.74 billion from $2.56 billion as passenger revenue increased 8 percent, although cargo income declined by 1.5 percent.

Northwest said its results were hurt by the re-imposition of the 10 percent federal tax on airfares and a 32 percent jump in the cost of jet fuel, which helped boost expenses by more than 6 percent. It added that it expected these factors to continue to impact the company for the rest of the year.
The Minneapolis-based airline, which flies a number of Pacific routes, said its results were also hurt by the strength of the dollar against the Japanese yen.
For the first nine months of the year, Northwest said its net income soared 50 percent to $510.1 million, or $5.49 a share, from $338.5 million, or $3.79 a share.
Revenues for the year to date rose 9.5 percent to $7.54 billion from $6.88 billion as passenger revenue grew by 12 percent while cargo income slipped by almost 3 percent.
Northwest's stock gained $1.25 to $31.75 in late morning trading on the Nasdaq market.
